title: Constructed integral realization reindexing comparison
statement: Fix a prime l, an arbitrary scheme isomorphism g:X→Y with l invertible on both schemes, normalized native realizations R,S, RingReindex B, a finite coefficient field E and IntegralReindex I at E. The literal equalities of pullback with finite-stage inclusion and integral localization, followed by R.integral, inverse completion-unit comparison, inverse I.derived and inverse S.integral, construct a natural isomorphism from Q_E ⋙ inclusion_E ⋙ commonStageDerivedPullback(g) ⋙ ordinary(R) to Q_E ⋙ inclusion_E ⋙ ordinary(S) ⋙ derivedPull(B). Every factor is a specified map, not an arbitrary witness.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15 and Proposition 6.8.14, pp. 61–62; Hemo–Richarz–Scholbach Lemma 7.9, p. 22. Explicit assembly of the corresponding finite-coefficient subargument.

proof.text: The normalized common-stage pullback is the functor of its coherent stage morphism. The generic inclusion-map formula gives equality of its composite with a stage inclusion and the finite rational pullback followed by inclusion. The integral-object and pure-tensor equations of rationalDerivedPullback similarly prove equality before and after integral localization.

proof.text: The natural and constructibly invertible map podCompletedToTower restricts to a natural isomorphism on integral constructible objects. Whisker its inverse by scalar extension, compose with inverse I.derived, and conjugate by R.integral and S.integral. Whiskering the two functor equalities supplies the literal object transports. For the component calculation use their object equalities; proof irrelevance identifies these with the separately prescribed localization object equations. Every factor is a natural isomorphism. Prove the literal component agreement using the abstract heterogeneous component formula and the equality-map transport lemma. Store that proof together with the constructed isomorphism in IntegralRealizationReindexData, keeping its large constructor irreducible and exposing the comparison by a small projection.
